newsitem.title: DUBAI: PRESS DIGEST - United Arab Emirates - Sept 15.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - United Arab Emirates - Sept 15.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the United Arab Emirates press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- UAE foreign minister calls for Cairo economic conference to be held in November.
Egypt has said that it might postpone until next spring the conference if negotiations between Israel and the Palestinians do not make enough progress soon.
- Japanese official predicts increase in Japanese trade with UAE due to falling yen.
- The United States sends 5,000 troops to Kuwait.

- Nine Arab financial markets boost performance in second quarter of 1996. Saudi, Omani and Kuwaiti trading rises while activity falls in Bahrain and Tunisia, Abu Dhabi-based Arab Monetary Funds says.
-Thai trade delegation visits Dubai Chamber of Commerce to discuss ways of boosting trade.
- Arab League blasts interference in Iraq.
- Shipping circles fear hike in hull insurance rates in the event of another missile attack on Iraq.
- Japan remains the UAE's main trade partner. Volume tops $1 billion in first half of 1996.
- Arab League backs the UAE in its territorial dipute with Iran over three Gulf islands.
- Privatisation in Gulf remains a far cry.
- Japanese cars sales to UAE begin to pick up with a 30 percent rise in sales in first five months of 1996.
